D005-D007_h001.question:
It started around six months ago. I’ve had depression on and off for years, but this time it’s been almost constant—most days I wake up feeling like there’s no point. I drag myself to the lab, but I can’t focus on the code or the robots; I just stare at the screen, thinking everything is pointless. I’ve stopped tinkering with my side projects, barely see friends, and even with my wife I feel numb and withdrawn. Sleep is lousy—either I’m up half the night or sleeping 11–12 hours and still exhausted. I feel guilty, like I’m letting my team and my family down.

About two months ago, things got…different. I became convinced something catastrophic is coming, like the world is literally disintegrating. It doesn’t feel like a metaphor—I *know* it’s happening. I see cracks in the sky, buildings kind of “melting” at the edges, shadows moving that no one else reacts to. For a couple of weeks early on, those visions and this certainty about the world ending were there even when my mood strangely lifted a bit—I wasn’t as sad, but the sense that reality was breaking stayed. Since then the depression came back and has been there most of the time alongside the weird experiences.
D005-D007_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h002.question:
I guess this started around two months ago. At first I was just really down, like a heavy kind of depression. I stopped caring about work; I’d sit in the studio staring at the board, not actually mixing anything. I feel worthless most days, like there’s no point, and I sleep way too much but still wake up exhausted. I’ve pulled away from friends, stopped answering calls, and I barely eat unless I force myself.

Around that same time I started getting this weird thing where I taste metal or chemicals in my mouth, like someone spiked my drink or food, even when I haven’t eaten anything. It makes me think someone’s trying to poison me. I’m convinced people at the studio have hidden mics or cameras on me, like they’re tracking what I do and say. I’ll check the room for equipment, unplug things, but I still feel watched.

There was a stretch, maybe two or three weeks, when the low mood sort of lifted, but the bad tastes and the feeling of being monitored kept going, just as strong. Then the depression came back and has been there most of the time since.
D005-D007_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h003.question:

Sometimes I’m interpreting in a quiet classroom and suddenly I “taste” bleach or blood. No one else notices anything, but it feels so real that I have to swallow repeatedly or drink water to cope.

Most of these two months I’ve felt intensely low—heavy, hopeless, barely any energy. I drag myself to assignments, then just lie in bed afterward. I’ve lost interest in things I used to enjoy, even signing with friends. For a couple of weeks in the middle of this, the weird tastes and conviction about my body kept going even though my mood was more or less neutral. Then the depression came crashing back, and it’s been there more days than not since this all began.
